games.title: Six games, one board culture
games.sub: Each one teaches a different way of thinking — and every one is playable right now, no account required.

gomoku.name: Gomoku
gomoku.blurb: Two colours, one grid, five in a row. The rules fit in a sentence; the tactics do not. Best entry point if you have never touched a Chinese board game.

xiangqi.name: Xiangqi
xiangqi.blurb: A river cuts the board in half. Cannons only capture by jumping over a screen. The two generals may never look at each other down an open file.

go.name: Go
go.blurb: You surround territory instead of capturing a king. Still played under essentially the same rules it had two millennia ago.

reversi.name: Reversi
reversi.blurb: Flip the board in your favour. A handful of stones can swing the whole game — easy to learn, brutal to master.

chess.name: Chess
chess.blurb: The western classic, fully playable: castling, en passant and promotion, against a sharp alpha-beta engine. One board, infinite lines.

tsumego.name: Tsumego
tsumego.blurb: Go life-and-death puzzles. One correct move captures the group — train the reading that wins real games.

ladder.title: Eighteen rungs, borrowed from the real thing
ladder.sub: Chinese board culture ranks players in grades and dan, not in bronze and platinum. We kept that, and mapped it onto a rating that actually moves when you win.

howTo.title: How to Play
howTo.sub: YiBoard has six games. Each card below links to the rules and a live board you can play instantly.
howTo.rule1: Black plays first. Players alternate, one stone per turn.
howTo.rule2: Stones go on the intersections of the grid, not inside the squares.
howTo.rule3: A stone never moves and is never captured once placed.
howTo.rule4: The first player to line up five stones of their colour — horizontally, vertically or diagonally — wins immediately.
howTo.rule5: If the board fills with no five in a row, the game is a draw. In practice this almost never happens.
howTo.openingTitle: Three things that will make you better today
howTo.tip1Body: A single open three can be blocked. Two open threes that share a stone cannot — your opponent only gets one move. Almost every game is decided by the first double threat.
howTo.tip2Title: Count the open ends, not the stones
howTo.tip2Body: Three stones with both ends free is far stronger than four stones walled off at one end. Learn to see the gaps before you see the line.
howTo.tip3Body: Beginners answer an open three. Stronger players answer an open two when it points at a strong direction. If you are always reacting, you have already lost the initiative.
howTo.notationBody: Columns run A to O from the left; rows run 1 to 15 from the bottom. The centre point is H8. We use this in shared games and in your history.

about.title: About YiBoard
about.lead: Chinese board games are not hard to learn. They are hard to find in a form that respects your time.
about.p1: Most places that teach Gomoku, Xiangqi or Go want an account before you can see a board. Then a download. Then a tutorial you cannot skip. We think that ordering is backwards: play first, decide later whether you care.
about.p2: So YiBoard opens with a live board on the front page. No email, no install. The engine runs locally, your progress lives in this browser, and if you ever want it on another device you attach an email and nothing else changes.
about.p3: Gomoku ships first because it is the fastest way to feel why these games are good. Xiangqi comes next — a real strategic game with pieces most people outside China have never used. Go last, because it deserves to be done properly.
about.p4: We are a small team. If something is broken, or a translation reads badly in your language, tell us and it gets fixed in the next release.
about.shopBody: We are working on a small line of well-made physical sets — Xiangqi in wood, Go stones in glass. Not merchandise with a logo on it. Details when they are ready.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: We collect as little as possible. This policy says what we collect and why.
privacy.s1Body: On your first visit we write an anonymous guest identifier (a JWT, valid 180 days) in your browser to keep your record and rating. We do not collect your name, location or device details unless you attach an email.
privacy.s2Body: Attaching an email is optional and only syncs your record across devices. Passwords are stored as argon2 hashes; we cannot read your plaintext password.
privacy.s3Body: We do not sell your data, do not serve personalised ads, and do not track you across the web.
privacy.s4Body: To delete your account and game history, email ahmedlzany423@gmail.com and we will process it within 30 days.
privacy.s5Body: Only the guest identifier and a language preference cookie. No third-party analytics.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.sub: Can't find an answer? Email ahmedlzany423@gmail.com.
faq.q1: Do I need an account to play?
faq.a1: No. Open the board and play — your progress is saved in this browser for 180 days. Attach an email only when you want it on another device.
faq.a2: Three levels: Gentle (2-ply), Steady (4-ply), Sharp (6-ply). It runs alpha-beta search under a 500 ms budget, in your browser.
faq.q3: How do I play a friend?
faq.a3: On the Play page pick "Against a friend", create a room, and send the code or link. They join straight onto the board, no account needed.
faq.a4: Friend matches settle ELO, mapped to the eighteen grades and dans from Ninth Grade to Ninth Dan. Everyone starts at 1200 (Sixth Grade). Engine games do not move your rating.
faq.q5: How long is my data kept?
faq.a5: Guest records last 180 days. With an email attached they are kept until you ask us to delete them.
faq.a6: Payments are being integrated (later phase). Everything is free until then, and we will announce before launching.
faq.a7: YiBoard is a responsive web app (PWA planned), so it plays in any mobile browser with no download.
